To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the systematic prevalence of flourishing conditions within an institution depends largely on how the organization has evolved.

(i) the prevalence of intrinsic motivation in an institution is dependent on the extent to which it can be experienced in the institution; (ii) the extent to which that is possible is determined by how the work of the institution impacts the beneficiaries of that institution; (iii) the impact of the work of an institution on beneficiaries is a function of the degree to which it is new; and (iv) the extent to how new the work is is a function of its age.
the evolution of organizational institutions is driven by a tension between exploration of the new and positive impact on beneficiaries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how organizational evolution affects the extent to which institutions can foster human flourishing.
how the evolution of institutions can lead to their institutionalization, and how the latter can lead to the loss of the conditions for flourishing.
the evolution of organizational institutions, and the extent to which they support human flourishing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more an institution has been around, the more likely it will be to be controlled by vested interests and the less it will be able to support the flourishing of its members.

the prevalence of flourishing in an institution requires the prevalence of intrinsic motivation, which requires exploration and positive impact, which requires the absence of hierarchies and vested interests.
the evolution of organizational institutions is characterized by a shift from mass flourishing to vested interests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of organizations from exploration to exploitation leads to a shift from flourishing to vested interests, with the latter being a major source of the former.
the institutional conditions that support flourishing are not the same as the conditions that support vested interests.

the evolution of organizational institutions is characterized by the transition of flourishing conditions from being experienced by the whole institution, to being experienced by only a part of the institution (i.e., those who are in contact with beneficiaries), and finally to being experienced by none of the institution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, to flourish, organizations need to find ways to support their frontline staff to experience the impact of their work on their beneficiaries.

the conditions for flourishing in institutions are not only about the design of the institution itself but also about the conditions under which it emerges and the extent to which it is able to sustain a positive impact on the beneficiaries it is supposed to serve.

the conditions for flourishing are more likely in the early stages of organizational evolution, and that the institutionalization of the conditions for flourishing can be a key driver of organizational evolution.
